text: Eritrea tends to be a very welcoming, open society, especially once you get to know people. C onversations often start with lengthy greetings, how is your family, friends, how is wor k, etc. At initial meetings these questions may include which town are you from. It is customary to spend some time asking about one’s family and work, after which you can be very direct in communicating. It is best to avoid speaking about religion, politics and the war with , until a strong relationship has been established. Once you get to know people, you will generally find that the will be more comfortable to open up and speak candidly.

Less than an arm’s length of personal space tends to be the norm during conversations. Between men and men and women and women it may be even less. It is common to see men hold ing hands with other men while walking and talking. This is a sign of friendship T ouching while talking is accepted for men with men and women with women , but between genders there is usually no touching and more personal space given .

Direct eye contact is common among friends and family. During initial meetings it may be appropriate to avoid excessive eye contact as it could be interpreted as disrespectful. Looking away or down during conversations is generally viewed as a sign of respect and admiration to the speaker.

Transportation services do not tend to run on time. M eeting s and gatherings rarely start on time even though as a foreigner it is polite to be punctual. In rural areas, very few people have watches and/or clocks.

The guerilla war, where many women were fighters, changed attitudes and liberalized the roles of women to a certain degree. That being said, there are still defined roles for women such as keeping the house, raising the children, and for the most part women were not free to socialize in bars with men or other women. In rural areas, the only women out at night, in bars, tended to be the working women (waitresses/barmaids/prostitutes). Most women who are seen out a night get a bad reputation. This can be true with foreign women as well.
To beckon someone it is common to hold the hand with palm down and curl fingers into the hand quickly in a scratching motion. Raising your eyebrows during conversations generally means ‘yes’.
Avoid showing the bottoms of feet, soles of shoes, and moving or touching objects with the feet w hen interacting with Eritreans who are Muslims or follow Islam.

The legal drinking and purchasing age i s 18 and is not heavily enforced . There are strict laws against homosexuality; punishable by imprisonment. Penalties for possession, use, or trafficking in illegal drugs are severe, and convicted offenders can expect long jail sentences and heavy fines.

For Men - A suit is common for formal business situations. Generally, business casual attire is appropriate. In rural areas, khakis and a nice collared shirt are usually acceptable. For Women - A suit is common for formal business situations. Generally, business casual attire is appropriate. It is best to avoid sleeveless attire and skirts that are knee length or above. Jeans, shorts, and very revealing clothing are generally not appropriate in business situations.

At initial meetings it is best to use "Ato" (Mr.) , "Weizero" (Mrs.), or Weizerit (Miss) followed by the person’s first name not the last. When dealing with government officials and other professionals like doctors, it is best to use their title. It is customary to wait to be invited to call someone solely by their first name.

It’s best to show up on time for a meeting even though you may end up waiting. It is best to pay respect to the highest ranking person in the room and then follow accordingly. Always start with the requisite greetings – how are you, how is your family, how is work, etc. This can go on for minutes before getting down to any business The person who is hosting the meeting should open and close the meeting.

Decisions tend to be made from the top down. In the market place, negotiat ing and h aggl ing is expected . It’s common practice . to over-act, act offended, act surprised, walk-away three times, joke, etc., while negotiating a price.
In social situations, if invited to someone’s house or meeting someone for the first time, it is best to bri n g a gift. S ugar, tea, coffee, or something small but useful is a good choice.

Dress at most u niversit ies is somewhat like business casual attire . Long pants, nice jeans or dress pants for men and dresses or pants for women. More casual clothing like shorts , flip-flops, or ragged t-shirts are generally not acceptable. Lecture is the most common form of teaching. Grades are given on an A-F scale, with F being failing.

Students socialize by going to the movie theater, coffee shops, occasional soccer matches and having social gatherings/parties at student houses. Drinking is not really acceptable for students although it certainly occurs. Few, if any, students smoke as it is expensive and generally not socially accepted by their peers. It is not acceptable for students to be drunk in public. Dating rituals tend to vary among ethnicities and religion. Public displays of affection like walking hand in hand or anything like that is generally not acceptable.
